create.name: Upright Noble Zen
create.bio:
Upright Noble Zen is a small Zen community in Anchorage, Alaska, that practises both in person and online. It is led by Dana Kojun Lederhos-Hull, a Zen teacher based in the city who spent fourteen years in full-time monastic training and has led retreats in California, the Pacific Northwest, British Columbia and Alaska. In 2012 she became the first dharma successor of Jan Chozen Bays and Hogen Bays, teachers in the line of Taizan Maezumi, and she belongs to the Soto Zen Buddhist Association and the White Plum Asanga. The group describes itself as a place where committed practitioners and curious newcomers of any faith or none can explore Zen together.

The heart of the week is the Sunday evening programme at the Anchorage Pioneer Schoolhouse, also streamed on Zoom: two periods of sitting, a dharma talk, a short check-in and closing chants. Online zazen with the Heart Sutra runs early on five mornings a week, with further online sittings on Tuesday and Thursday evenings. Silent one-day zazenkai and multi-day sesshin are held through the year, mainly in person, and more than a hundred short talks by Kojun can be heard free as a podcast.

courses.title: Zen Retreat: Zazenkai and Sesshin
courses.description: Silent one-day and multi-day retreats with long periods of zazen, chanting, mindful meals and sometimes a talk and private interview with the teacher, held in person with an online option mainly for people outside Anchorage. Some prior practice with the group is generally expected.
courses.price: Suggested contribution $40 to $60 per day in person ($30 to $50 if online)

courses.title: Sunday Evening Program
courses.description: The community's main weekly gathering at the Anchorage Pioneer Schoolhouse and on Zoom: two sitting periods, usually a dharma talk and check-in, and closing chants. Recommended as the first event for newcomers.

free_resources.title: Morning and Evening Sitting Schedule
free_resources.description: Open Zoom sittings at dawn from Sunday to Thursday with Heart Sutra chanting, and evening sittings on Tuesdays and Thursdays closing with the Song of Zazen.

free_resources.title: Dharma Talks
free_resources.description: A page pointing to Kojun's podcast of more than 130 short dharma talks, free to stream on several listening platforms.
